items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: That was before Alvin Alcorn went in there.

ctx.x: When you had, before you got them false teeth, Gilbert Youngkin playing the side, either side or the middle. He had all these games. He'd get tired. He'd play. You ever get tired there, he'd play. I'm with you all over his mouth. Yeah, I was seeing him get his lip all bust up and he said, well, who's stopping him from playing?

He said, I've got more lip. He was another one of those jitney men. You know, he'd been there. He was on the jitney a long time with Earl Foster too. Right over there on the canal at the Alamo. Yeah, that was before Alvin Alcorn went in there. He went and got young this day.

So far, this sounds like a trumpet lesson. There's one more question I have to ask before we move on to your life again. Did Mr. Matoy ever say anything about breathing, anything special, exercises on breathing or anything that he gave you?
